passages.note: Roll call 58 lists Garten among the 28 Yea votes on SB 1(ss), a single-subject abortion bill.

passages.provision_quote: before the earlier of viability of the fetus or twenty (20) weeks of postfertilization age of the fetus, if: (A) for reasons based upon the professional, medical judgment of the pregnant woman's physician, if either: (i) the abortion is necessary when reasonable medical judgment dictates that performing the abortion is necessary to prevent any serious health risk to the pregnant woman or to save the pregnant woman's life; or (ii) the fetus is diagnosed with a lethal fetal anomaly;
passages.note: Enrolled SB 1(ss) permits abortion before viability/20 weeks only for a serious health risk, to save the mother's life, or a lethal fetal anomaly diagnosis.

passages.provision_quote: if: (A) the pregnancy is a result of rape or incest;
passages.note: Enrolled SB 1(ss) permits abortion in the first ten weeks only when the pregnancy results from rape or incest.
Bill tracking page names Glick as author and McNamara/King as sponsors; it names no act by Garten, so (like an encyclopedia page pointing to a roll call) it cannot support his chair.

rows.reasoning: Garten voted Yea on SB 1(ss) (2022ss), a single-subject abortion bill whose enacted text makes abortion unlawful except for the circumstances it names, including when "the pregnancy is a result of rape or incest" and when necessary to prevent "any serious health risk to the pregnant woman or to save the pregnant woman's life," matching the rung "ban abortion except in cases of rape, incest, or a serious risk to the mother's life."
